analysis:
Examined all supplied test source, patches and file metadata. Changes add test-only residency/lease setters (AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift:120-126) and selected-model recovery fixtures and suites; no concrete security regression is supported in this scope. Tests specify withdrawing an expired nonselected adoption before draining and eviction (SelectedModelPlacementPolicyTests.swift:31-46), protecting selected models, holds, dwell, leases and pins (SelectedModelRecoveryVictimTests.swift:124-201), backing off memory refusals, serializing residency mutations, and cancelling recovery under add-on holds (SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests.swift:99-230). SelectedModelRecoveryTests.swift:17-60 exercises startup/capacity paths with scripted loaders. These expectations principally concern A-018, TB-007, TB-012, T-029 and T-059; they do not establish production enforcement.
Integration must inspect the recovery implementation and its admission, unload and load interactions: verify withdrawn models cannot accept or reload new work while existing requests drain, victim checks remain valid across suspension, and real native loads cannot publish residency after an add-on hold. The cancellation test explicitly uses a cooperative Task.checkCancellation() stub (SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests.swift:213-216), so native cancellation and final publication fencing remain unverified, not observed missing controls. Also reconcile load-gate identity verification with T-027 and SSD reservation release/model bindings with T-041 during eviction/reload. Nothing supplied changes encryption, credentials, attestation, billing or cache format; these tests do not validate those dependencies. Production recovery and the referenced UnreclaimableLoadMemoryFixture are outside this supplied source scope, leaving material cross-file availability conclusions for integration.
